Take home Exercise 1 : Geospatial Analytics for Public Good

Author

Priya

Published

September 13, 2025

Modified

September 24, 2025

1 Overview

Here’s a fresh pass in my own voice—same analytical spine, but tightened and a touch more conversational. We’re looking at where and when new firms pop up in Singapore across four SSIC groups between 1 Jan 2024 and 30 Jun 2025:

  • 36 — Water collection, treatment & supply
  • 51 — Air transport
  • 56 — Food & Beverage service activities
  • 93 — Sports, amusement & recreation

Plan of attack (short + sweet): - Clean ACRA (dates/SSIC/postcodes), then geocode via OneMap.
- Map quick counts by planning area/subzone to set the scene.
- Do KDE for first‑order intensity (common breaks so maps are comparable).
- Run nearest‑neighbour + spatio‑temporal diagnostics to see if timing piles on top of place.
- Slice monthly ST‑KDE to spot what’s emerging, steady, or fading.
- Wrap with planning notes per sector—what to protect, where to manage, and how often to check in.

CRS sanity: OneMap’s X/Y are already SVY21 (EPSG:3414). Build points directly in 3414. No pre‑transform detours.

2 Data

2.1 Sources

Dataset Purpose Format Provider Notes
ACRA – Information on Corporate Entities (A–Z, Others) New registrations by date/SSIC CSV (27 files) data.gov.sg / ACRA Alphabetical split (A–Z + Others)
SSIC 2020 Sector classification lookups CSV/XLSX SingStat We derive ssic2, ssic3
OneMap Search API Postal geocoding to coordinates Web API SLA / OneMap Returns WGS84 + SVY21
Master Plan Subzones (MPSZ 2019 No Sea) Analysis/join window KML → GPKG URA/SLA Reprojected to EPSG:3414

If you have MPSZ 2024, swap the file path & label below; methods are unchanged.

2.2 Fields used (ACRA)

uen, entity_name, registration_incorporation_date, primary_ssic_code, postal_code, entity_type, status.

2.3 Study window & scope

  • Time: 2024‑01‑01 → 2025‑06‑30 (inclusive).
  • Space: Singapore outline; aggregation by planning area/subzone.
  • Sectors (ssic2): 36, 51, 56, 93.

3 Setup — packages, folders, seeds

if (!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")
Loading required package: pacman
pacman::p_load(
  # core
  tidyverse, dplyr, readr, stringr, purrr, lubridate, janitor,
  # geo
  sf, tmap, terra,
  # stats / PP
  spatstat, spatstat.geom, spatstat.explore, splancs,
  # viz / tables
  plotly, gtsummary, classInt, viridisLite,
  # api
  httr,
  # optional speed
  vroom, data.table
)

set.seed(626)
options(scipen = 999)

# folders
aspatial_dir <- "data/aspatial"
geo_dir      <- "data"
rds_dir      <- "data/rds"
rasters_dir  <- "data/rasters"
dir.create(rds_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(rasters_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
